subject: Struggling with introducing conditions to a model

messages.author: 8da5b06c56385794
messages.subject: Struggling with introducing conditions to a model
parts:
Hello,

I'm sure I'm doing something silly wrong, as I've done similar things before without difficulty. The model of interest concerns consecutive bernoulli trials, where the probability of success decays exponentially. Here is the original model:

data {
    int N; // number of trials
    int success[N];
    int x[N]; // time position of trial
}

parameters {
    real <upper=0> rate;
}

model {
    real theta;
    for (i in 1:N) {
        theta <- exp(rate * x[i]);
        success[i] ~ bernoulli(theta);
    }
}

This works fine. However, there are actually many different conditions in my data, such that each trial belongs to a condition with a slightly different rate. I've been trying to modify my model to take this into account. Here is the modified model:

data {
    int<lower=0> N; // number of trials
    int<lower=0,upper=1> success[N];
    int<lower=0,upper=N> x[N]; // time position of trial
    int<lower=0,upper=N> M; // number of conditions
    int<lower=0,upper=M> t[N]; // which condition this trial is from
}

parameters {
    real <lower=-10, upper=0> rate[M];
}

model {
    for (i in 1:N) {
        success[i] ~ bernoulli( exp(rate[t[i]] *  x[i]) );
    }
}

As you can see, I've upped the constraints significantly. But I'm still getting an initialization error:

Initialization failed after 100 attempts.  Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model.

If I drop the lower constraint on the rate parameters, I get a similar error, except that it attempts to initialize to NaN and fails.

I'm very confused as to why this is problem. I intend to introduce a hyperparameter on the rate parameters when I get this working, but as of right now shouldn't this be equivalent to fitting the first model M times (once for each condition)?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Struggling with introducing conditions to a model
parts:
There are a couple of things that could go wrong here.
But if you're not getting any kind of report, there's something
wrong with our reporting.

If t[i] = 0, the index to rate[t[i]] will be out of bounds --- Stan
indexes from 1.

Are you trying to provide an initialization yourself? Is it between
-10 and 0 and not on the boundary? Boundaries will underflow and
overflow.

The only other issue I could see coming up in this model is a value
of x[i] = 0 with a corresponding success[i] = 0.

If none of those is the problem, would you mind sharing your
data so we could debug further?

- Bob

messages.author: 8da5b06c56385794
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Struggling with introducing conditions to a model
parts:
It seems there is no nice way to get data in Python into the format used by stan_rdump. However, if you are comfortable using PyStan, it is quite easy to load the data there. Here is a program that will load the data and compile/run the model:

model_string = """

data {
   int<lower=0> N; // number of trials
   int<lower=0,upper=1> success[N];
   int<lower=0,upper=N> x[N]; // time position of trial
   int<lower=0,upper=N> M; // number of conditions
   int<lower=0,upper=M> t[N]; // which condition this trial is from
}

parameters {
   real <lower=-10, upper=0> rate[M];
}

model {
   for (i in 1:N) {
       success[i] ~ bernoulli( exp(rate[t[i]] *  x[i]) );
   }

}
"""

import json
import pystan

dat=json.load(open('/path/to/file.json','r'))
model = pystan.StanModel(model_code=model_string)
fit =model.sampling(data=dat,iter=1000,chains=1) #Can change iterations and chains, obviously

rjson appears to be fairly well-recommended on StackOverflow, and the code snippet is short:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2617600/importing-data-from-a-json-file-into-r

The data is all single-dimensional.
On Thu, Feb 13, 2014 at 2:21 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

If someone could recommend a reliable reader in R for JSON,
I could probably use that, too.   If there are multidimensional
objects I might bail.

- Bob


On 2/13/14, 7:45 PM, Filip Krynicki wrote:

I will read up on the Stan dump format and try and get it to you in that.


On Thu, Feb 13, 2014 at 1:05 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com <mailto:ca...@alias-i.com>> wrote:

    Is there an easy way to convert JSON data with PyStan into
    the Stan dump format?  Is PyStan reading JSON?  I really
    need to study up more.  But as is, I don't know how to handle
    JSON.

    - Bob


    On 2/13/14, 5:19 PM, Fil Krynicki wrote:

        I have checked for all the the potential errors you identified. I tightened the bounds a little to not allow 0
        for t, I
        do not provide an initialization, and there is no x = 0 success = 0 coincidence.

        A JSON dump of the data is attached. Also, I am using pystan 2.1.0.

        On Wednesday, February 12, 2014 6:06:32 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:

             There are a couple of things that could go wrong here.
             But if you're not getting any kind of report, there's something
             wrong with our reporting.

             If t[i] = 0, the index to rate[t[i]] will be out of bounds --- Stan
             indexes from 1.

             Are you trying to provide an initialization yourself?  Is it between
             -10 and 0 and not on the boundary?  Boundaries will underflow and
             overflow.

             The only other issue I could see coming up in this model is a value
             of x[i] = 0 with a corresponding success[i] = 0.

             If none of those is the problem, would you mind sharing your
             data so we could debug further?

             - Bob

             On 2/12/14, 11:28 PM, Fil Krynicki wrote:
              > Hello,
              >
              > I'm sure I'm doing something silly wrong, as I've done similar things before without difficulty. The
        model of
             interest
              > concerns consecutive bernoulli trials, where the probability of success decays exponentially. Here is the
             original model:
              >
              > |
              > data {
              >      int N; // number of trials
              >      int success[N];
              >      int x[N]; // time position of trial
              > }
              >
              > parameters {
              >      real <upper=0> rate;
              > }
              >
              > model {
              >      real theta;
              >      for (i in 1:N) {
              >          theta <- exp(rate * x[i]);
              >          success[i] ~ bernoulli(theta);
              >      }
              > }
              > |
              >
              > This works fine. However, there are actually many different conditions in my data, such that each trial
        belongs to a
              > condition with a slightly different rate. I've been trying to modify my model to take this into account.
        Here is the
              > modified model:
              >
              > |
              > data {
              >      int<lower=0> N; // number of trials
              >      int<lower=0,upper=1> success[N];
              >      int<lower=0,upper=N> x[N]; // time position of trial
              >      int<lower=0,upper=N> M; // number of conditions
              >      int<lower=0,upper=M> t[N]; // which condition this trial is from
              > }
              >
              > parameters {
              >      real <lower=-10, upper=0> rate[M];
              > }
              >
              > model {
              >      for (i in 1:N) {
              >          success[i] ~ bernoulli( exp(rate[t[i]] *  x[i]) );
              >      }
              > }
              > |
              >
              > As you can see, I've upped the constraints significantly. But I'm still getting an initialization error:
              >
              >     Initialization failed after 100 attempts.  Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained
             values, or
              >     reparameterizing the model.
              >
              >
              > If I drop the lower constraint on the rate parameters, I get a similar error, except that it attempts to
             initialize to
              > NaN and fails.
              >
              > I'm very confused as to why this is problem. I intend to introduce a hyperparameter on the rate
        parameters when I
             get
              > this working, but as of right now shouldn't this be equivalent to fitting the first model M times (once
        for each
             condition)?
              >
              > --

- Bob

parts:
I've been taking some more stabs at figuring this problem out, attempting to specify initial values for the rate parameters.

I tried supplying an M-length array of -1s, but this causes the following error:

RuntimeError: Rejecting user-specified initialization because of vanishing density.

With no more information. I understand this should appear only when the initial value is directly on the boundary (-10 and 0 in my case). But, given that my constraints are purely negative, and the initial values are inverse-logit transformed to (0, 1), how can I specify initial values in this range?
